content.text: {"answer":"Content creators can understand why their items are not being recommended by using provider-facing transparency and observability tools that separate system behavior from raw outcome signals. One approach is to train a surrogate or proxy model that approximates an item’s exposure distribution and then quantify which item features most influenced exposure or lack of exposure across the user base; this explains system-level drivers of visibility and can reveal that the important factors differ by recommender model and domain [1]. Another approach is counterfactual observability: instead of relying on views and clicks alone, estimate what the recommender would have done and what engagement would have followed without a specific item or model decision, helping attribute poor exposure to model behavior, bias, presentation, audience reach, or content effects [2].\n\nRelated work differs in focus. Pairwise counterfactual explanations answer comparative questions like why one item ranked above another by tracing ranking differences back to items in a user profile [4]. Work on familiarity bias shows that structural exposure imbalances can suppress emerging creators, suggesting one concrete reason items may be under-recommended in video systems [7].","grounded":true}
